sentences.text: Uberabasuchus possessed a high, triangular skull with a moderately narrow snout and large, round eye sockets.
Its lower jaw held at least twelve teeth, with the third tooth being the largest, followed by nine smaller ones of roughly equal size.
The third tooth in the lower jaw was significantly larger than the other nine teeth.
The species name U. terrificus combines the city of Uberaba with Greek and Latin words meaning crocodile and terrible.
The species was described based on specimen CPPLIP 630, a skull with jaws and a partial postcranial skeleton found in Minas Gerais, Brazil.
Evidence from its skeleton and the arid climate suggests Uberabasuchus was likely a terrestrial predator.
Uberabasuchus is classified within the family Peirosauridae.
This animal lived from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
Later analyses contradict the hypothesis that Uberabasuchus is closely related to Mahajangasuchus, indicating they belong to different groups: Sebecia and Mahajangasuchidae respectively.
